grammar_rules.rule_name: Main clause verbs followed by que
grammar_rules.summary: Verbs in the main clause of indirect speech are followed by que (où, si, etc.); the dependent clause is usually indicative.
grammar_rules.explanation: A list of typical main clause verbs is provided: affirmer, annoncer, assurer, avouer, confier, constater, crier, déclarer, dire, expliquer, observer, prétendre, promettre, remarquer, répondre, révéler, s'apercevoir, savoir, se rendre compte.
grammar_rules.formation: [main clause verb] + que / où / si + [dependent clause in indicative]
restrictions: Limited to main clause reporting verbs such as dire, affirmer, annoncer, savoir
The dependent clause is usually in the indicative, not the subjunctive
Que is replaced by si when the dependent clause is an indirect yes/no question
exceptions: si replaces que for indirect yes/no questions
The subjunctive appears when the main verb itself requires it
agreement_rules: Each verb agrees with its own subject in person and number; main clause and dependent clause agree separately.
The conjunction que is invariable and does not affect the agreement of the dependent clause.
grammar_rules.word_order: main clause verb + que / où / si + dependent clause in indicative
transformations: Je ne sais pas si elle viendra.
Il m'a expliqué où il habitait.
